in a cohort of patients at risk for cardiovascular disease the risk of cardiovascular outcomes is increased above the cut-off values of 5.5 mg/dl in women and 5.9 mg/dl in men.

in a large cohort of patients with cardiovascular disease, hyperuricemia is an independent risk factor for the primary outcome of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke, and that this risk is increased at uric acid values >6 mg/dL, which is lower than the cut-off currently used to define hyperuricemia.
